No. `opened` is a post-treatment variable. It can only be 1 for customers who received the email, so it is a consequence of the treatment. Controlling for it would condition on something the treatment affects. That would introduce selection bias, because the customers who open emails differ systematically from those who don't, and it would also block part of the effect we want to measure. The email was randomly assigned, so a simple comparison of mean payments between the email and control groups already gives an unbiased ATE. Adjusting for pre-treatment covariates such as `credit_limit` and `risk_score` is fine if we want more precision, but `opened` should be left out.

ANSWER: no
